method: The RFC 6298 algorithm keeps two running values from each round-trip sample. The first sample R sets SRTT to R and RTTVAR to R/2; each later sample R' moves RTTVAR to three quarters of its old value plus one quarter of the gap between the old SRTT and R', and only then moves SRTT to seven eighths of its old value plus one eighth of R' - in that order, because the variation update uses the old smoothed value. The timeout is SRTT plus max(G, 4 x RTTVAR), where G is the clock granularity and K = 4, and RFC 6298 rounds any result below one second up to one second. This page starts the timer at the RFC 6298 initial value of 1000 ms, applies the one-second floor after every sample, and optionally caps the result at 60000 ms, the minimum maximum the RFC allows. One to 24 samples are accepted, each from 0 to 60000 ms, separated by spaces, commas, semicolons or line breaks; the granularity is accepted from 0 to 1000 ms and defaults to 1 ms. The page reports the plain average, SRTT, RTTVAR, the timeout before the floor, the applied floor and cap flags, the initial 1000 ms timer and the timeout after each sample, so the smoothing can be followed step by step. A single sample, a floored result, a capped result, a variation above half the smoothed value and a zero-millisecond sample each raise a warning rather than a refusal. The timer modelled is the measurement-driven one: a real sender doubles it on each retransmission until a good sample arrives, and implementations differ in the maximum they keep. Times are shown to 0.001 ms. The page runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.
